question: Should the sensor node move from a moving-average filter to an IIR low-pass?
author: analyst (role)

sources.title: Filter unit tests (C and Python twins)

findings.claim: The 4-sample moving average was chosen for integer-only math and testability; weak roll-off was an accepted trade.
The control loop uses about 8 % of its 10 ms budget, so a heavier filter is affordable on timing grounds.
Existing tests pin exact integer outputs (C-style truncation); any new filter needs new golden values in both twins.
No open tracker item requests better filtering; the open high-severity work is power (sleep mode).
findings.note: Absence of a request is not evidence of no need.

open_questions: What vibration spectrum does the deployment actually see? No field data is in the repository.
Does the host already filter, making node-side changes redundant?
recommendation: Keep the moving average for now. Revisit only if field data shows aliasing above 10 Hz; prioritise sleep mode (SN-CAP-001) first.
next_steps: Capture 60 s of raw IMU data from a bench unit and attach an FFT to this brief.
If a change is warranted, prototype the IIR in sim/sensor_node/filter.py behind the same API and update ADR-0001.
